a3556.speech: Visited Cabo Delgado this month and described the situation in northern Mozambique as a neglected crisis: “Climate shocks, increasing violence and spiralling hunger are having a terrible impact on the population.”

a3786.speaker: International Research and Exchange Board (IREX), USAID implementing partner
a3786.speech: Is calling for collective efforts from the government and development partners to reform traditional practices in order to end Gender-Based Violence in the country.

a3786.speaker: Linet Omwange, IREX Chief of Party
a3786.speech: Suggested that all people including parents, caretakers and children must all advocate to reduce GBV in their communities ; underscored that it is women and girls who are the most affected by gender-based violence in the country, and called for awareness campaigns to educate society on the need to eliminate negative cultural norms that perpetuate GBV ; “With the work that we do through the media, the youth can be reached, so that they can understand the importance of reducing the numbers of GBV that are mostly as a result of the cultural practices that we practice” ; “But also the economic situations that we do go through, why do we have early marriages, why do we have other practices that do not support equality between men and women, the young girls and the boys is because of some of the situations that we find ourselves in” ; “All of us here have a responsibility to be able to work against and curb those traditional practices that bring about harmful behaviors” ; “While we acknowledge that GBV is not just about the women being abused, the numbers and the statistics do [show] that it is actually women and girls who are much more affected by GBV.”

a3786.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a3786.speech: Reveals that it has documented 6,779 gender-based violence cases in South Sudan since 2015, and discloses that the most reported forms of GBV are physical assault and psychosocial or emotional abuse ; its incident report released last week showed a 30% increase in GBV cases in 2024, marking a slight but concerning rise over the past six years (2018-2024), with women and girls most affected and 30% of survivors being children, primarily adolescent girls, and the highest number of rape cases reported in Western Equatoria, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Central Equatoria ; emphasized the need for more robust prevention, risk mitigation, and response mechanisms, particularly in underserved areas.

a3852.speaker: United Nations
a3852.speech: says that almost 5.2 million people in Mozambique are in need of assistance due to a “triple crisis” comprising “armed conflict and displacement, recurring extreme weather events, and months of post-electoral unrest”.

a3852.speaker: Xavier Creach, coordinator and deputy director for West and Central Africa of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a3852.speech: stressed that the situation is particularly dire in Cabo Delgado province. Said that the activity of non-state armed groups has increased displacement and the destruction of infrastructure, also hampering recovery efforts. More than 25,000 Mozambicans in the north of the country have been forced to flee their homes in recent weeks due to the escalation of the conflict ; “Thousands have lost their homes, many for the second or third time, and are seeking safety in already overstretched communities.” ; said protection concerns, including gender-based violence, family separation and limited access to documentation, are rising sharply.

a3852.speaker: Xavier Creach, coordinator and deputy director for West and Central Africa of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a3852.speech: warned that the humanitarian crisis in Cabo Delgado has already left 1.3 million people displaced and could worsen due to a serious funding gap for vital aid operations; warned of the risk of some “vital programmes” being abandoned if “urgent support” is not mobilised for Mozambique ; “A perfect storm is gathering. If we turn away now, the country will face a much larger humanitarian emergency. The crisis is unfolding now. We have a choice. We can act to prevent, support and protect – or we can sit on our hands.”

a3852.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) (statement)
a3852.speech: estimated that more than 3.4 million Mozambican children require urgent support and called for a scaled-up humanitarian response to the growing needs in the country ; “Mozambique is facing multiple challenges that have further aggravated the humanitarian crisis in the country. More than 3.4 million children are in need of urgent humanitarian assistance.” ; armed conflict in Cabo Delgado province and extreme weather events “have left the country very vulnerable”, causing “outbreaks of infectious diseases and the destruction of schools and health facilities”.

a3852.speaker: Unicef Portugal
a3852.speech: has launched “an urgent appeal for donations to support emergency operations in Mozambique and guarantee a future for these children and their families”.

a3884.speaker: Ousainu Darboe, UDP Party Leader and Secretary General
a3884.speech: In a stirring address, lauded the diaspora's unwavering support, describing their contributions as a cornerstone of the UDP's vision for a democratic and prosperous Gambia. "Your commitment is not only appreciated-it is inspiring," Darboe declared. "This support sends a strong signal that the UDP is not just a national force, but a global movement committed to democratic progress and national development."

a3884.speaker: UDP official (anonymous)
a3884.speech: Emphasized the strategic importance of the diaspora's role, stating, "This is just one of several fundraising events planned by the party-both in the diaspora and within The Gambia-as we prepare for 2026." The official noted that the Seattle convention's success would bolster the party's ability to mobilize voters and expand its reach in the lead-up to the elections.

a3884.speaker: Talib Ahmed Bensouda, Mayor of Kanifing Municipality
a3884.speech: Delivered a compelling speech praising the diaspora's organizational prowess and urging continued engagement; called on supporters to sustain their momentum, emphasizing the importance of a united front as the UDP prepares to challenge for the presidency.

a3884.speaker: Landing B. Sanneh, Chairman of the Mansakonko Area Council, Lower River Region
a3884.speech: Echoed this sentiment, highlighting the diaspora's role in amplifying the party's message of inclusive governance and national development.

a3889.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3889.speech: Addressing State House correspondents on Wednesday, described the operation as the largest in the agency's history, undertaken to curb the distribution of falsified medical products and safeguard public health.

a3889.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3889.speech: Urged the National Assembly to expedite amendments to the NAFDAC Act and the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods Act to include life sentences and the death penalty for offenders. "With the signing into law of the Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA), assets recovered from suspects will be treated as proceeds of crime after their conviction by the courts," she added.

a3889.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3889.speech: Noted that the operation forms part of the agency's National Action Plan (NAP 2.0) for 2023-2027, aimed at strengthening regulatory enforcement and consumer confidence in pharmaceuticals; explained that planning for the highly confidential exercise began in 2024 in collaboration with the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA). ; Noted that the exercise, originally planned for one week, had to be extended by two to three weeks in each location due to an underestimation of the scale of violations: "The NSA duly informed the respective Governors to ensure a buy-in. However, the exercise had to be extended by an additional two to three weeks in each of these locations because it was underestimated during the planning phase."

a3889.speaker: NAFDAC (agency)
a3889.speech: According to NAFDAC, the agency screened over 7,000 shops, leading to the removal of falsified medicines and the arrest of more than 40 individuals. ; NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting Nigerians from the dangers of counterfeit and substandard medicines.

a3889.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3889.speech: Said the seized products were discovered stacked in toilets, under staircases, and on rooftops at very high temperatures, without consideration for cold chain storage requirements. ; On TAFRADOL, a drug recently banned in India after an undercover BBC investigation exposed its illicit export to Africa: "This drug combination has not been licensed anywhere in the world and is outrightly banned for use in the European Union," she said.

a3889.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3889.speech: On the relocation of drug markets to Coordinated Wholesale Centres: "The current premises occupied by medicine sellers are unregistered and unregistrable," Mrs Adeyeye stated, adding that the locations fail to meet basic standards for drug storage, sales, and distribution. ; She said the seized consignments of banned, expired, unregistered substandard and falsified medical products will be destroyed simultaneously publicly in each of these locations after the exercise.

a4073.speaker: Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re, Dean of the College of Cardinals
a4073.speech: In his homily, acknowledged the presence of representatives from various parts of the world who had come to the Vatican to pay their respects to Pope Francis.

a4073.speaker: Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re, Dean of the College of Cardinals
a4073.speech: Spoke about Pope Francis, saying: "He had a firm humanity in the leadership of the Church and he was a Pope among the people, with a heart open to all." He said the Pope favoured the poor, refugees and displaced people; that mercy and joy were two important words he emphasised in his papacy, alongside the importance of fraternity; and that Pope Francis raised his voice for peace without ceasing and insisted on building bridges, not walls.

a4073.speaker: Vatican News (website)
a4073.speech: According to it, even during Pope Francis's funeral, as happened 20 years ago at the funeral of Pope John Paul II, the wind opened the pages of the Book of the Gospels and made them turn above the coffin, all of which happened in St Peter's Square immediately before and during the sprinkling of water by Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re and the incensing.

a4073.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice President of Tanzania
a4073.speech: Said the best way to honour Pope Francis is to uphold peace together with caring for the poor ; said the Pope was humble and a man who made great efforts in the search for peace in various parts of the world and left a mark, including the episode of kissing the feet of South Sudan's leaders so that they would abandon fighting ; said that among the last documents the Pope signed was a letter he wrote to the President of the United Republic of Tanzania wishing her a happy 61st anniversary of the Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.

a4073.speaker: Office of the Vice President of Tanzania (statement)
a4073.speech: Said Dr Mpango made those remarks after the Mass had ended.

a4073.speaker: Pope Francis (spiritual testament, written 29 June 2022)
a4073.speech: Asked that his tomb be placed in the chapel of Our Lady, Health of the Roman People, and that his tomb be dug in the ground, simple, without special ornamentation, bearing only the single inscription “Franciscus.”

a4201.speaker: Edward Lama Wonkeryor, Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a4201.speech: “This policy means we are committing ourselves to fostering environments where students, faculty, and staff can thrive without fear of discrimination, prejudice, or marginalization” ; said the DEI policy document would ensure that policies and practices across Higher Education Institutions are designed with equity at the forefront—addressing disparities that may exist in access to education, resources, and opportunities ; “It will also ensure that our curriculum and pedagogy reflect the richness of Liberia’s diversity, preparing our graduates to contribute meaningfully to both the local and global communities” ; “The policy guidance compliments the National Commission on Higher Education’s aspirations for excellence in tertiary education. Inclusive institutions prevent discrimination, enhance fairness, promote equal opportunity, and provide support services for staff, students, and other educational sectors” ; said under this policy, no students shall face discrimination based on gender, disability, ethnic origin, cultural background, political affiliation, religion, marital status, or age, noting that the DEI policy is not just a set of ideals but a blueprint for the future of higher education in Liberia ; “It acknowledges that equity ensures everyone has access to the same opportunities regardless of their background is not just an aspiration but an obligation. It emphasizes inclusion, creating democratic spaces where an individual feels valued and empowered to contribute to our academic community” ; explained that in the context of Liberia, a country rich in cultural diversity, the policy document was not just timely but also essential, and called on Liberian institutions to reflect the plurality of the society ; asserted that the true power of education can only be fully realized when it is inclusive, equitable, and representative of the diverse populations it serves ; “The DEI Policy Document we are launching today is a tangible testament to our collective commitment to ensuring that our higher education system in Liberia embodies these principles. This is especially critical in higher education, where we are not just shaping individuals but shaping the future leaders, innovators, and change-makers of our nation.”

a4201.speaker: Edward Lama Wonkeryor, Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a4201.speech: “We are deeply grateful to USAID/TESTS for their partnership in this endeavour. Their support underscores the global commitment to building education systems that serve every student, regardless of their background or circumstances” ; “As the Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education, I pledge our full support in this endeavour. We will work closely with all Higher Education Institutions to ensure that the principles of diversity, equity, and inclusion are embedded not just in policy but in practice and foster dialogue, encourage best practices, and hold ourselves accountable to the standards we are setting today.”

a4201.speaker: Cllr Cooper W. Kruah, Minister of Labor, Liberia
a4201.speech: Said in the continuously evolving world of education, policy and governance was an integral component of effective leadership, and stressed that developing a deep understanding of policy and governance structures was essential for aspiring educational leaders ; “The Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) policy, a collaborative initiative of the NCHE and USAID, through the TESTS project, actually aims at ensuring a gender-free and inclusive learning environment to induce the acquiring of quality learning objectives by students in Liberia. The policy complements NCHE’s reform initiatives to promote quality and excellence in tertiary education across universities and colleges in Liberia” ; “institutions are encouraged to prevent discrimination, enhance fairness, promote equal opportunity, and provide support services for staff, students and other educational stakeholders in our country” ; “Under this policy, no student shall face discrimination based on gender, ethnic origin, disability, cultural background, religion, political affiliation, marital status. By these standards, students at our tertiary institutions, are therefore expected to maximize their learning without any hindrance, whatsoever. Further, engaging in policy development and reform is an effective means of bolstering the impact educational leaders have on those they serve.”

a4264.speaker: Dr Kweku Anane Gyinde, corporate governance expert and lecturer at the GIMPA Law Faculty
a4264.speech: Said that while taxes are vital for national development, rolling them out without adequate consultation risks undermining public support: "As an institution, if you want to make any decision or regulation, your intention is not to punish the people but to ensure compliance. It's important to engage the public beforehand so they have time to adjust, understand the need for it, and support it" ; "It's not too late for the government to return, engage, and sensitize the people, because all this unrest does not help the country."

a4264.speaker: Dr Kweku Anane Gyinde, corporate governance expert and lecturer at the GIMPA Law Faculty
a4264.speech: Said he could not confirm whether the government had engaged the public ahead of the levy's introduction, but noted that the controversial E-Levy had left many Ghanaians wary of sudden policy announcements.

a4264.speaker: Zakaria Tanko Musah, communications specialist and legal practitioner
a4264.speech: Acknowledged that while taxes are often unpopular, meaningful dialogue can help the public accept them: "The engagement should have started before the passage of the law in Parliament" ; "Given our experience with the E-Levy and the promises made by the government, it would have been more prudent to offer some sort of pre-engagement and explanation" ; "The choice of words in the engagement is also very crucial."

a4264.speaker: Zakaria Tanko Musah, communications specialist and legal practitioner
a4264.speech: Said the rationale behind the new levy, expected to help clear a US$3.1bn debt in the energy sector and maintain stable electricity supply, is sound, but cautioned that a lack of consultation could deepen public mistrust.

a4290.speaker: Martin Luther (1517), refusing to recant before the Catholic Diet of Worms
a4290.speech: “Here, I stand accused. I can do no other.”

a4290.speaker: John the Baptist (Matthew 3:11)
a4290.speech: “I indeed baptise you with water into repentance, but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, …he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire.”

a4290.speaker: The Bible (Romans 12:15), biblical edict cited
a4290.speech: “Mourn with those that mourn. Rejoice with those that rejoice…”

a4290.speaker: Dr. Frank Amoakohene, Ashanti Regional Minister
a4290.speech: Blurted out at the fire scene: “Are you afraid to tell me there is no water in the tender? Don’t lie to me… Take the tender away if there is no water in it… what is it doing here…? Why are you standing there idle…?”

a4290.speaker: Alex King Nartey, National PRO, Ghana National Fire Service
a4290.speech: Noted: “He (the Regional Minister) could have easily just approached any of our officers or the commander without necessarily hasting to put a camera on himself to create a spectacle. To what end? Because at Kantamanto there was no shouting but we were able to quench the fire. So, what was the essence of the shouting with the cameras there, just to create a scene that you are working. One of our officers fell from the top and is at the hospital right now. We don’t have health insurance, we don’t have any height allowance… The President himself acknowledged the effort of the firefighters and came to say thank you. Any thanks from the honourable Minster? There was nothing; he just wanted to criticize our men and then demoralize them…”

a4290.speaker: Simon Osei-Mensah, former Ashanti Regional Minister
a4290.speech: Charged at the school feeding caterers in April 2023: “I didn’t become a Minister to pamper people who engage in lawlessness… so long as I continue to be the Regional Minister anyone who goes on a demonstration without informing the police, we will deal with that person as the law prescribes. We won’t tolerate lawlessness. If your child comes to you with chants in demand for a favour will you be happy?”

a4290.speaker: President John Dramani Mahama (May 2014 address to NDC sympathizers in Kumasi)
a4290.speech: “…The Presidency is working hard so don’t allow anyone to deceive you into thinking that we are retrogressing… As I speak, there are several projects ongoing. Roads, water and electricity… runways of the Kumasi Airport … GIHOC footwear. However, the Akans have a saying that the chicken never pleases the hawk no matter how well it dances …. As for Kumasi, even if we construct roads tarred with gold, they will tell us that we did nothing…”

a4290.speaker: President John Dramani Mahama
a4290.speech: Consoled the victims, pledging government support, and charged the security to do thorough investigation and report to him. He noted: “We must take fire safety seriously. Cooking in the market, especially with gas and cylinders poses a serious risk. Preventing such disasters must be a shared responsibility…”

a4290.speaker: Daniella Ntow Sarpong, Acting Head of the Ghana National Fire Service / Chief Fire Officer
a4290.speech: Did a “mea culpa”: “I refer to the uncomplimentary comments and remarks by a member of the Public Relations Team… On behalf of myself (?) and the entire Ghana National Fire service we unreservedly extend our profound and sincerest regret for any unfortunate comment made against your good self and reputable office as the Regional Minister and Chair of REGSEC…”

a4290.speaker: Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia
a4290.speech: Offered GH¢200,000 plus a promise of 1,000 bags of cement.

a4387.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) for Africa
a4387.speech: Declared that the objective of the memorandum of understanding signed on Thursday is to promote growth ; “We are here to move forward further after the results recorded for the first Compact with respect to access to justice, land and finance” ; said the lack, insufficiency or continued unavailability of electricity remains a major obstacle to growth ; “There is a programme that is being implemented to remedy this,” indicating that an envelope of 250 million dollars, approximately 125 billion CFA francs, will be devoted to it ; “This will be the solution to these problems; I remain confident that with the leadership of the ministers present here, of the coordinator of the UCF/MCA and of the President of the Republic, the life of the population will be improved.”

a4387.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) for Africa
a4387.speech: Indicated, following the signing of the memorandum, that the agreement in principle settles the institutional and policy framework of the energy sector, which will ultimately make it possible to increase the supply of electricity for businesses and households in Benin ; remarked that this requires a framework and a regulation of budgetary resources to make the investments sustainable, enabling the government to move forward in order to avoid interruptions in the supply of electrical energy ; said there will be reforms that will establish and guarantee the sustainability of investments for operational and technical purposes, and that it will be more possible to do business in the sector, which was lacking previously ; explained that the Board of Directors of the MCC will meet in the meantime to endorse the proposals made by the experts.

a4387.speaker: Komi Koutché, Beninese Minister of the Economy, Finance and Denationalisation Programmes
a4387.speech: “This day is memorable for the Beninese government; I salute our American friends and all the other actors who have worked so that we could arrive at these results” ; remarked that MCA is a trophy and went on to say that the first Compact made it possible to move many lines, the journey having been long but enriching ; “We are making the commitment that we will carry out the reforms meticulously and will do everything for them to succeed,” he promised.

a4427.speaker: U.S. State Department / President Donald Trump (executive orders)
a4427.speech: Based on orders signed by President Donald Trump, the US State Department stopped the disbursement of funds from the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), a programme for HIV treatment in Nigeria and other developing countries, for at least 90 days.

a4427.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4427.speech: Granted a waiver allowing PEPFAR to continue providing life-saving HIV medications to low-income countries.

a4427.speaker: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a4427.speech: Called for enhanced global collaboration to combat the spread of Mpox, which was earlier declared a continental and global health emergency, and is scaling up response by expanding laboratory capacity, deploying rapid-response teams, and intensifying vaccination campaigns in hotspots.

a4427.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Welfare (Nigeria)
a4427.speech: “the form is an instituted measure to prevent the spread, monitor the possible importation of infectious diseases and aid the control of disease outbreaks, thereby protecting the health of all Nigerians.”

a4427.speaker: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)
a4427.speech: Noted that the National Lassa fever multi-partner, multi-sectoral incident Management System has been activated to coordinate response at all levels at the Emergency Operation Centre (EOC); highlighted challenges including late presentation of cases leading to increased CFR, poor health-seeking behaviour, poor environmental sanitation conditions and poor awareness in high-burden communities.

a4427.speaker: Nigerian government
a4427.speech: Said it is focusing on large-scale treatments against Neglected Tropical Diseases, and had in November said approximately $19 million is required to effectively combat NTDs in the country.

a4427.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a4427.speech: Has pledged to ramp up domestic resource mobilisation efforts to ensure the sustainability and ownership of Nigeria’s HIV/AIDS response, in light of President Donald Trump’s decision to halt overseas assistance programmes.

a4427.speaker: President Donald Trump
a4427.speech: Said the US withdrawal from the World Health Organisation was due to the inappropriate political influence of member states on the global health body.

a4427.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4427.speech: Called for a constructive dialogue with the US, emphasising the need to preserve their decades-long partnership; said its relationship with the US is pivotal to protecting global health and security, noting the country played a significant role in efforts to tackle disease outbreaks, strengthen health systems and respond to emergencies in challenging environments; said it will in the interim review some of its programmes, reduce travel expenses and freeze recruitment, except in critical areas.

a4434.speaker: Industry stakeholders (property sector, Malawi)
a4434.speech: Have warned that Malawi’s property market faces a potential downturn as aid withdrawal by development partners, including the United States government, leads to project closures and weakens demand for office space.

a4434.speaker: Edmund Hami, Mpico Board Chairperson
a4434.speech: Revealed on Friday that the aid freeze is already reducing disposable incomes and could lead to widespread retail closures, despite the company maintaining a 92 percent occupancy rate: “Our properties include retail, office and residential spaces. In all these areas, it is about people’s disposable income, so if traffic to our retail facilities falls, that could affect us because retailers may be forced to close.”

a4434.speaker: Edmund Hami, Mpico Board Chairperson
a4434.speech: Acknowledged the residential gap but declined to commit to immediate intervention, saying that the company’s retail and office investments align with its long-term strategy ; disclosed that the company is exploring diversification into tourism and mining to align with broader investment strategies.

a4434.speaker: Purity Chitalo, Central Region Chairperson of the Minority Shareholders of Listed Companies
a4434.speech: Praised Mpico’s “strategic direction”, saying the growth plans “excite shareholders” despite market uncertainties.

a4550.speaker: Friend of the author's brother (young man who had been investing in Ethiopia for 10 years)
a4550.speech: “This is my last trip to Ethiopia, I am done” ; “Ethiopia has potential everyone can see but very few can touch.”

a4550.speaker: USAID Fact Sheet (2017)
a4550.speech: According to the USAID Fact Sheet from 2017, youth unemployment in Ethiopia is estimated at nearly 27 percent.

a4550.speaker: An acquaintance of the author (planning an illegal journey through Libya)
a4550.speech: Mentioned to the author his plans to make an illegal journey through Libya, and mentioned the night school degree he had been working on and how he was not paid enough at his current job. “I thought getting this degree was going to change things for me.”

a4746.speaker: Action Against Hunger (international NGO)
a4746.speech: Told AFP on Tuesday that the impact of US aid cuts has already taken a toll in South Sudan, and that children are dying.

a4746.speaker: Doctors Without Borders
a4746.speech: Said Tuesday that the Abyei region in northwest South Sudan was the latest to see a cholera outbreak, with more than 330 cholera cases recorded in June thanks to a “critical” lack of water and sanitation facilities.

a4746.speaker: The Lancet (British journal)
a4746.speech: Said on Tuesday that the cuts to USAID could lead to more than 14 million deaths globally by 2030, including over 4.5 million children under the age of five.

a4746.speaker: Denish Ogen Rwot, Action Against Hunger’s communication and advocacy lead in South Sudan
a4746.speech: “I think it’s not just a fear. It’s already a reality. We’re already having some mortality rates coming in” ; “Already we are having children die” ; estimated they had lost 30 per cent of their funding due to the USAID cuts ; “That means now we’ll have facilities without food… and how do we work without these supplies?” ; “We are running on sheer faith.”

a4812.speaker: Officials of the Société d’exploitation du guichet unique du Bénin (Segub)
a4812.speech: Explained that an enormous loss of time is still observed at the Port of Cotonou, since it takes about fourteen days, accompanied by harassment of all kinds, to complete administrative formalities, and that with the dematerialisation reform all documents, now computerised and gathered under the name of single administrative documents, should make it possible to go from fourteen days to one or two working days.

a4812.speaker: Rufin Nansounon, Minister of the Maritime Economy of Benin
a4812.speech: Said the project is placed at the centre of the government’s strategies for the structural modernisation of the country, and that it strengthens Benin as a key regional player over the long term.

a4812.speaker: Thierry Verdier, Director General of Segub
a4812.speech: Said that arrangements had been made to integrate the different parameters that had raised concerns (the mechanism for sending documents, the legal value of dematerialised documents, the narrowness of the export network, the international legal environment) ; had also promised that his company would work in symbiosis with all the stakeholders in order to make the system as efficient as possible.

a4812.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin
a4812.speech: Said that beyond the tools, work must be done to expand production capacity, which is indispensable to increasing the export margin.

a4812.speaker: Is-Dine Bouraima, Director General of the Guichet unique de formalisation des entreprises (GUFE)
a4812.speech: Presented the outlines of the new reform aimed at reducing the time needed to formalise a business from 8 hours to one working hour, and specified that to succeed a number of preconditions must be settled, among them strengthening internet connectivity and the dematerialisation of all related documents.

a4833.speaker: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces
a4833.speech: tweeted in 2022, then UPDF Commander Land Forces: "It wouldn't take us, my army and me, 2 weeks to capture Nairobi."

a4833.speaker: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces (@mkainerugaba on X)
a4833.speech: "The USA owes at least $100 billion for our work in Somalia. We did alot better than the people in Ukraine. It seems their speciality is running from Russians. We are waiting for payment." ; "$100 billion is the minimum I demand from the USA. And they will pay every penny! Fast and in a hurry! On top of that they'll invite me to visit the US Army...soon." (August 16, 2024)

a4833.speaker: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces
a4833.speech: posted a tweet critical of Presidential advisor and brother in law Odrek Rwabogo, that he deleted soon after.

a4833.speaker: Yoweri Museveni, President of Uganda
a4833.speech: said in a statement: "I ask our Kenyan brothers and sisters to forgive us for tweets sent by General Muhoozi," adding that public officers should not interfere in the affairs of other countries; the President however added that, "I know for a fact that General Muhoozi is a passionate Pan-Africanist. However, the correct method for Pan-Africanists is confidential interactions or using the available forums."

a4847.speaker: Dr Akpan Nse, Director of Port Health Services, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Nigeria
a4847.speech: Stated on Friday, September 5, 2025 that the new wave of the Ebola virus has led the Federal Government to tighten the movement of people across Nigerian borders ; noted that additional staff had been employed to strengthen border surveillance in the country.

a4847.speaker: Dr Akpan Nse, Director of Port Health Services, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Nigeria
a4847.speech: Noted that although Nigeria was at risk of importing the virus due to high levels of international travel with the DRC, Port Health Services was on alert and had strengthened surveillance to prevent this ; "We have intensified surveillance at all points of entry across the country—airports, land borders, and seaports. Every inbound traveller coming from Congo to Nigeria is thoroughly screened, and we collect their medical history through mandatory forms. We have also reactivated our portals. Every passenger on every flight coming to Nigeria from Congo is screened upon arrival. This applies to airports, seaports, and land borders. Even if passengers transit through Congo on their way to Nigeria, they must undergo screening."

a4847.speaker: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo
a4847.speech: Declared an outbreak of Ebola virus disease in Kasai Province, where 28 suspected cases and 16 deaths, including four health workers, had been reported as of September.

a4847.speaker: National Institute of Biomedical Research, Kinshasa (laboratory test results)
a4847.speech: Samples tested on September 3 confirmed that the cause of the outbreak was Ebola Zaire, a strain of the Ebola virus.

a4847.speaker: Oladipo Kolawole, Associate Professor of Infectious Diseases and Genomics, Department of Microbiology, Adeleke University, Osun State
a4847.speech: Warned that Nigeria should not let down its guard to prevent the importation of the virus ; while he expressed confidence in Nigeria's expertise in handling the situation, he also called for coordination among various ministries, departments, and agencies to ensure an effective response ; "Everybody coming into the country, especially from DR Congo, must declare where they are coming from at the point of entry, and we must keep our surveillance system well-tightened. I think there is a bit of awareness about the virus in the country, and I'm very sure that all the institutions are on ground to handle things based on the experience we had previously on Ebola. I believe the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention has a structured system in place that can handle that, and now they have expanded their lab to Lagos. The Nigerian Institute for Medical Research is also available in that regard, and they have a good structure to handle it."

a4847.speaker: Dr Moses Adewumi, virologist, Department of Virology, College of Medicine, University College Hospital, Ibadan
a4847.speech: Emphasised the urgent need to activate surveillance systems to protect individuals and ensure that preventive measures were fully enforced to stop the virus from entering the country ; stressed the importance of putting in place all necessary procedures to strengthen the country's preparedness.

a4912.speaker: Many experts (unnamed)
a4912.speech: In the view of many experts, the crisis in the Sahel is one of the most neglected crises in the world.

a4912.speaker: UNICEF (statement published in September 2022)
a4912.speech: According to a UNICEF statement published in September 2022, more than 11,100 school establishments had been forced to close their doors across the Sahel region.

a4912.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4912.speech: Reports that 35% of health centres in conflict-affected areas are partially or totally non-functional.

a4912.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a4912.speech: Highlights the dramatic impact of conflicts on access to care, stressing that malnutrition and infectious diseases represent major health risks for thousands of children.

a4912.speaker: United Nations and several humanitarian organisations
a4912.speech: Are launching an urgent appeal to the international community to protect children's rights in the Sahel, and international actors propose a support plan resting on several essential axes.

a4912.speaker: UNICEF
a4912.speech: Has formulated a request for 150 million dollars intended to intensify educational support programmes and promote the reintegration of child soldiers, a sum considered vital to finance projects to secure schools, restore damaged infrastructure and strengthen local education capacity.

a4912.speaker: Local authorities
a4912.speech: For their part, are calling for better coordination between the governments of the countries concerned and international organisations, with protection mechanisms adapted to the specificities of the field, including strengthened security around educational centres and health structures and monitoring arrangements to prevent the recruitment of children by armed groups.

a5269.speaker: Stephen Abamfo, Greater-Accra Regional Education Director
a5269.speech: At the ceremony, emphasised the importance of reading, which he described as the gateway to imagination and knowledge. "When we open a book, we are not just reading words but rather, we are embarking on an adventure that can transport us to different worlds," he said. He further stated that books held "hidden treasures" in the form of lessons on culture, history and the human experience. He, therefore, urged young readers to explore various genres and uncover those riches.

a5269.speaker: Dr Ivy Asantewa Owusu, Eastern Regional Education Director
a5269.speech: Emphasised that reading and understanding formed the foundation for a child's learning across all subjects. "If a child cannot read and understand well, their foundation is weak. This applies to all subject areas, including mathematics and science," she said.

a5269.speaker: Survey conducted by the West Africa for Worldreader in 2023
a5269.speech: Revealed that only seven per cent of students had books at home for reading purposes in Ghana.

a5269.speaker: Dr Ivy Asantewa Owusu, Eastern Regional Education Director
a5269.speech: Appealed to parents to take reading seriously and buy books for their children, revive the practice of evening reading sessions, and encourage the use of libraries among their children. "We are using this platform to appeal to parents that they should take reading seriously. They should buy books for their children," she said.

a5272.speaker: Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario
a5272.speech: "Believe me when I say that I do not want to do this. I feel terrible for the American people," said the Premier of Ontario, Doug Ford, arguing that "there is one person who is responsible, President Donald Trump," he added. To that end, the regional leader ordered the Independent Electricity System Operator to add 10 Canadian dollars to the price of each megawatt exported to the United States.

a5272.speaker: Government of Ontario (Doug Ford's government)
a5272.speech: Indicated that it expects to collect up to 400,000 Canadian dollars a day from the surcharge, and that this amount "will be used to support Ontario's workers, families and businesses."

a5272.speaker: Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario
a5272.speech: Had previously announced a ban on US companies bidding for public contracts offered by the province's government until the tariffs against Canada are lifted. "Every year, the government of Ontario [...] spends 30 billion dollars on contracts, not counting the 200 billion dollar plan to develop Ontario," he stated.

a5272.speaker: Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario
a5272.speech: Also warned that he would tear up a deal worth almost 100 million Canadian dollars with the internet provider Starlink, owned by Elon Musk, arguing that he "would not do business with people who are willing to destroy the economy."

a5272.speaker: Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario
a5272.speech: Said that the Liquor Control Board of Ontario (LCBO), the only authorised wholesaler of alcoholic beverages, would remove all American products from its shelves and catalogues to prevent commercial establishments and retailers from selling those products; the politician stated that the LCBO sold one billion Canadian dollars worth of spirits imported from the country to the south.

a5272.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5272.speech: Claims that the US does not need Canada.

a5292.speaker: Abi Mustapha-Maduakor, Chief Executive Officer, AVCA
a5292.speech: introduced the flagship forum by noting that despite a challenging macroeconomic environment in recent years, "Africa's private capital industry has remained resilient and will continue to rise." She reflected on AVCA's theme for the conference - "embracing change and shaping the next era of Africa's prosperity."

a5292.speaker: Phuthuma Nhleko, Chairman and Co-Founder, Phembani Group
a5292.speech: followed with an instructive keynote address rallying private investors to back innovative businesses to drive prosperity at scale. Reaffirming the region's competitive edge, he highlighted the imperative for policymakers, business leaders and investors to harness the fourth industrial revolution, powered by artificial intelligence (AI) and the digital economy ; argued: "the size of population generates 50 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP). By 2050, we will have 2.5 billion Africans that constitute over a quarter of humanity, with over forty per cent of youth below the age of 18. By this time, Nigeria's population is expected to be bigger than the US."

a5292.speaker: 'Tokunboh Ishmael, Co-founder and Managing Director, Alitheia Capital
a5292.speech: described the exponential growth witnessed throughout the second decade of private capital expansion in Africa.

a5292.speaker: Wale Adeosun, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Kuramo Capital Management
a5292.speech: aligned that Africa's private capital industry remains a nascent ecosystem with immense potential ; commented on the benefits of bringing institutional investors from the U.S into Africa.

a5292.speaker: Vincent Le Guennou, Chief Executive Officer, Africa50's Infrastructure Acceleration Fund
a5292.speech: proposed that the traditional private equity model replicated in the continent needs to be adapted and advocated for proactive efforts to attract the US$ 2.3 trillion of domestic capital in Africa that needs to be unlocked. He said: "This needs to be a key objective for the next 10 years."

a5292.speaker: Dieynaba Kamara, Partner and Chief Operating Officer, Joliba Capital
a5292.speech: expressed that most pension funds needed "education on investing in private equity as an asset class", especially in Francophone Africa where pension funds prioritise hard assets such as real estate.

a5292.speaker: Jerry Parkes, Chief Executive Officer, Injaro Investments
a5292.speech: re-emphasised the need to tap local pools of capital, drawing on Injaro's launch of Ghana's first private equity fund, anchored by Ghanaian pension funds.

a5292.speaker: Laurent Demey, Managing Partner, Amethis
a5292.speech: suggested that historically, "The big difference between liquidity in Africa and Europe or the US, has been that if you have a good business, you can sell it. In Africa, it has been a different story" ; he noted a shift in the industry with far more African companies and investors from emerging markets, such as the Gulf states or Turkey, making deals compared to traditional investors from the Global North.

a5292.speaker: Patrice Backer, Partner and Chief Investment Officer, AFIG Funds
a5292.speech: discussed the secondary market as a viable solution to liquidity constraints in African markets - attracting private finance yet to invest on the continent.

a5292.speaker: John Owers, Director and Head of Funds Solutions, British International Investment
a5292.speech: "A functioning private capital ecosystem needs to provide options for exits for Limited Partners (LPs), and that is what the secondary market does."

a5292.speaker: African Private Capital Association (AVCA)
a5292.speech: announced the winners of the association's 20th Anniversary Conference Awards, celebrating the outstanding firms and individuals championing private capital in Africa.

a5353.speaker: Allan Ngumuya, UTM NEC member and deputy Organizing Secretary 2018-2024
a5353.speech: Said the one candidate he was hoping for at No.1 was Madam Mary Chilima, but since it appears she is not coming forward, "I would like to endorse my other choice today"; endorses "DR DALITSO KABAMBE" and asks delegates to "give Kabambe your vote, and we shall never regret it. Trust me."

a5353.speaker: Allan Ngumuya, UTM NEC member and deputy Organizing Secretary 2018-2024
a5353.speech: Said that among all 4 candidates, Dr Kabambe, Dr Kaliati, Dr Mtumbuka and Engineer Kambala, there is none who could sell them off to any other party, that claims to the contrary are just campaign lies, and that each one's whole heart is with the UTM party and with carrying forward the vision of the late Dr Saulos Klaus Chilima, who was killed in the plane crash at Chikangawa on 10th June 2024.

a5353.speaker: Allan Ngumuya, UTM NEC member and deputy Organizing Secretary 2018-2024
a5353.speech: Urged delegates to choose a person who, when he wins the UTM presidency, will be able to run a strong campaign in 2025 and take the country; only the one who has the experience of having helped run the government of Malawi, who has genuine expertise, and who will be able to explain the failures of the MCP government and whom Chakwera will avoid debating.

a5353.speaker: Allan Ngumuya, UTM NEC member and deputy Organizing Secretary 2018-2024
a5353.speech: Said his endorsement should not create any enmity between him and those he has not endorsed, that there is no enmity toward the other contestants, and "Let us join hands to move our UTM party forward... No one is more perfect than another. The truth is we are all UTM."

a5377.speaker: Half-Yearly Report on the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, published by the Bank of Mozambique
a5377.speech: According to the report, export revenues from natural gas extracted in Mozambique were 901 million dollars during the first half of this year, growth of 33% compared with the same period of 2023. The report indicates that "the increase in natural gas revenues is explained by the rise in the volume exported, associated with the start of the exploitation and export of gas from Area 4 of the Rovuma Basin, in a context in which, on the international market, the average price fell by 28%."

a5377.speaker: Half-Yearly Report on the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, published by the Bank of Mozambique
a5377.speech: The document points to growth of 24 percent in the energy sector, resulting from the increase in production and tariff adjustments implemented by the exporting company for its main clients in the second half of 2023 and the beginning of 2024.

a5377.speaker: Half-Yearly Report on the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, published by the Bank of Mozambique
a5377.speech: On mineral coal, the decrease "was due mainly to the 32% fall in the average price on the international market," the document reads; on aluminium and heavy sands, the reduction "is a consequence of the contraction in production influenced by the equipment breakdown recorded in 2023."

a5377.speaker: Half-Yearly Report on the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, published by the Bank of Mozambique
a5377.speech: Data from the report indicate that Mozambique's net debtor position vis-à-vis the rest of the world worsened by 257.1 million dollars at the end of the second quarter of 2024 compared with the first quarter, with the balance standing at 71,524.9 million dollars.

a5377.speaker: Bank of Mozambique (central bank)
a5377.speech: Data published by the Bank of Mozambique indicate that "the Mozambican economy reduced its demand for financial resources from non-residents to finance its consumption and investment needs by 12.5%, with the combined balance of the current and capital accounts standing at 1,244.2 million dollars"; according to the financial institution, the negative result is due to the contraction of the current account deficit by 14.2 percent and the decrease in the surplus balance of the capital account by 39.0%. The document also states that "economic transactions between Mozambique and the rest of the world resulted in an overall surplus balance of 112 million dollars, which contributed to the increase in the monetary authority's reserve assets."

a5547.speaker: 2022 modelling study published in The Lancet HIV
a5547.speech: Found that with the CAB-LA jab, 52 000 new HIV infections can be stopped every year.

a5547.speaker: Researchers from the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation in Cape Town (demonstration study)
a5547.speech: Found that, among 1 084 people between 19 and 28 years old, 74% chose the injection.

a5547.speaker: Hasina Subedar, senior technical advisor for the national health department
a5547.speech: Told Bhekisisa at the conference that the jab, made by British manufacturer ViiV Healthcare, has been added to HIV prevention options at 16 research sites between February and June ; said that although it's too early to comment on trends from these studies, or draw clear conclusions, "the long-acting cabotegravir injection is gaining momentum as a popular choice among both young men and women."

a5547.speaker: Hasina Subedar, senior technical advisor for the national health department
a5547.speech: Says the 96 000 CAB-LA doses are enough for 13 728 people to use to protect themselves against HIV infection for one year.

a5547.speaker: Hasina Subedar, senior technical advisor for the national health department
a5547.speech: Says the 867 clinics chosen to stock Pepfar-sponsored CAB-LA have been selected because they've had a high uptake of oral PrEP - at least 20 new clients had to be given the pill in the past financial year ; said the department also had to ensure that the donations were given to at least one facility in each local municipality ; "If we run out of donations and, if there are no cheaper generic formulations, or the department has not been successful in securing CAB-LA at a lower price, we do have oral PrEP that is effective."

a5547.speaker: Sandile Buthelezi, Director General of the South African health department
a5547.speech: Says the government accepted the 96 000 CAB-LA doses, which will arrive between October and December this year, as part of a larger donation of 231 000 doses that Pepfar is releasing over two years ; says the department accepted the donation on the basis that cheaper generic versions of CAB-LA are likely to become available in early 2027, which will help the country to sustain supplies, so that people "don't have to stop and start."

a5547.speaker: Sandile Buthelezi, Director General of the South African health department
a5547.speech: Says other donors, such as the Global Fund for Aids, TB and Malaria, "also have shown appetite" to donate CAB-LA, and people started on this medicine will be able to switch to another injection, lenacapavir, which only has to be taken once every six months, should they choose to and if it becomes available in South Africa.

a5547.speaker: Recent study on lenacapavir
a5547.speech: Showed that none of 2 134 women who received lenacapavir contracted HIV.

a5547.speaker: Ashneil Jain, US State Department
a5547.speech: Said at an Aids conference session that Pepfar plans to sponsor CAB-LA in at least 12 countries before the end of the year.

a5547.speaker: ViiV Healthcare
a5547.speech: Said in November 2023 it will sell the medicine at £23.50 (about R555) a shot in 90 countries that the World Bank classifies as low- and middle-income, including South Africa, and also to donors.

a5645.speaker: Experts
a5645.speech: Say the move will likely exacerbate economic hardship in remittance-dependent countries like Somalia, Liberia, and El Salvador, many of which are already facing devastating aid suspensions ; warn that the tax could also undermine formal financial systems.

a5645.speaker: Center for Global Development (CGD)
a5645.speech: According to the CGD, the 3.5% tax could lead to a 5.6% drop in formal remittance flows, reducing household incomes and weakening consumer demand in low- and middle-income countries ; according to CGD projections, USAID cuts alone will shrink GNI by over 1% in 23 countries, including Somalia, where nearly 40% of previous U.S. aid has already been withdrawn ; according to CGD estimates, reducing remittance cost to 3% could offset over 50% of aid losses in 13 low-income countries, including Somalia.

a5645.speaker: World Bank (data)
a5645.speech: Shows that remittances to Africa totalled over $92 billion in 2024, with at least $12 billion originating from the United States.

a5645.speaker: Trump administration
a5645.speech: In early 2025 announced a near-total suspension of development assistance.

a5645.speaker: Research by Ahmed et al. (2021)
a5645.speech: Suggests a direct link between cost and behaviour: for every 1% increase in remittance fees, transfers fall by 1.6%.

a5645.speaker: Western Union (study)
a5645.speech: Found that a 5% remittance tax could reduce formal flows by 17.7% and increase informal flows by over 21%.

a5645.speaker: Development economists
a5645.speech: Argue that instead of taxing remittances, the U.S. and other donor nations should focus on lowering transaction costs ; also recommend policy measures such as matching grants to encourage the use of remittances in productive sectors, issuing diaspora bonds to channel capital into national infrastructure, and expanding seasonal work visa programs for residents of low-income countries.

a5785.speaker: Tanzanian Police Force (statement, September 9, 2025)
a5785.speech: Dismissed a claim circulating on social media that a body found floating at Jangwani, Dar es Salaam, on August 27, 2025, belonged to a government critic who had been strangled and dumped; said a team of major crime experts was dispatched to investigate the incident. “As the investigation continued, the relatives of the man were located and identified the body as that of Salehe Shukrani, a small-scale bread seller and resident of Magomeni Mikumi,” the police report stated. “They also confirmed that their relative suffered from epilepsy, a condition that had repeatedly caused him to collapse.” ; Emphasized that there were no signs of violence or foul play on the deceased, and urged members of the public to ignore the false claims, and to refrain from sharing or amplifying misinformation.

a5785.speaker: Kishindo (social media post/publication)
a5785.speech: Ran the headline: “Abdul and his squad abducted a journalist, strangled him, and dumped him in the Jangwani River.”

a5785.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a5785.speech: “We see on social media how some people ignore serious issues and instead attack your family. I remember during President Kikwete’s time, his son Ridhiwani was accused of owning everything. Everywhere you went, people would say, ‘This belongs to Ridhiwani,’” Chalamila said. “Madam President, I believe the same applies to you. These accusations will stop after your retirement—the lies will fade.”

a5839.speaker: United Democratic Front (UDF)
a5839.speech: Malawi's economic recovery is still a significant challenge, according to the United Democratic Front (UDF), acknowledging the nation's deep suffering.

a5839.speaker: Ismail Mkumba, UDF Spokesperson
a5839.speech: Reported that UDF has identified significant problems with the 2025-2026 fiscal year budget's emphasis on 'Consolidating Gains, Strengthening Resilience, and Inclusivity for Accelerated Social Economic Transformation' with apprehension. He said the party is not convinced that the economic transformation characterized by a 3.2% growth rate will be achievable. Mkumba added that the estimated inflation rate of 24% from the current 32.3% is rather unrealistic given the current high food inflation rate and an uncontrollable pricing regime which has held hard working Malawians at ransom. The legislator stated that they have taken note that the National Budget makes recurring incorrect assumptions about economic growth rates year after year, which has also been acknowledged by the Minister in his Budget Statement. "We are not convinced that the economic transformation characterized by a 3.2% growth rate will be attainable due to foreign exchange imbalances, unrealistic borrowing, and overreliance on foreign aid, among others."

a5839.speaker: Ismail Mkumba, UDF Spokesperson
a5839.speech: Expressed concern about the prolonged imbalance of foreign exchange reserves as a result of the limited capacity to export high-value goods and services. He lauded the latest measures taken by the Minister of Trade and Industry, Vitumbiko Mumbo, through the Prohibition Order of 2025 to reduce imports of products that can be produced locally.

a5839.speaker: United Democratic Front (UDF)
a5839.speech: The UDF feels that local producers have neither been equipped nor encouraged to meet the growing local demand for foreign goods and services, thereby endangering the very local consumers and industries that the government is trying to protect.

a5839.speaker: Ismail Mkumba, UDF Spokesperson
a5839.speech: Said overreliance on foreign sources to finance our development expenditure puts our budget in jeopardy, questioning independence attained in 1964 as we continue to rely on donors instead of developing mechanisms to finance the development of this sovereign estate through a surplus budget.

a5839.speaker: Ben Phiri, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Finance Spokesperson
a5839.speech: Said the 2025-2026 budget is a pack of lies and is a heap of senseless fiscal promises that will again not be delivered. Phiri said MCP wishes to continue with its fiscal deceit and budget hypocrisy. He adds that the 2025-2026 Budget has an economic context of MCP's broken promises and lies as Malawians were told by MCP that the economy would improve within 2 years. "Since June 2020, DPP has been providing constructive advice on how to manage the economy, but sadly the MCP chose not to listen, it opted to run the economy in their own MCP way, they deployed the new economic theory called SOSISA which was and I believe shall remain the most meaningless theory." He said the national budgets are also failing because MCP is making people borrow money from commercial banks at high interest rates with Reserve Bank policy rate of 26%.

a5966.speaker: Legislators, Eswatini House of Assembly
a5966.speech: Want Minister of Finance Neal Rijkenberg to conduct a post-clearance audit of selected pharmacies across the country to verify the sources of their drug supplies and ensure compliance with national laws.

a5966.speaker: Motion on a post-clearance audit of pharmacies (parliamentary motion)
a5966.speech: Seeks to establish whether pharmacies were adhering to all relevant Eswatini Revenue Service (ERS) regulations and import guidelines in the procurement and distribution of medicines ; According to the motion, Rijkenberg is required to table a detailed report within 60 days after the motion's adoption. The audit is intended to help detect any irregularities in the importation or clearance of pharmaceuticals, particularly cases where drugs may be entering the market without proper documentation or quality assurance.

a5966.speaker: Alec Lushaba, Hhukwini MP
a5966.speech: Said the motion aimed to strengthen oversight in the pharmaceutical sector and safeguard the public from illegally sourced or substandard medicines, while also ensuring that government does not lose revenue due to non-compliance with ERS requirements ; further noted that improving transparency in the pharmaceutical supply chain would not only protect consumers but also enhance the credibility of registered pharmacies operating lawfully within Eswatini.

a5966.speaker: Motion on the state-owned Pigg's Peak Hotel (parliamentary motion)
a5966.speech: Calls upon Minister for Tourism and Environmental Affairs Jane Mkhonta-Simelane to present a detailed report to the House on the current status of the state-owned hotel, to explain the measures the ministry was taking to improve the hotel's state and product offering in order to restore its reputation as a hotel of choice in the country's tourism sector ; directs the minister to address ongoing complaints about the poor state of the road network linking the hotel to the Matsamo and Ngwenya Border Posts ; gives Mkhonta-Simelane 14 days from its adoption to table a comprehensive report outlining the ministry's rehabilitation plans, marketing strategies, and infrastructure improvement projects related to the hotel and surrounding areas.

a5966.speaker: Alec Lushaba, Hhukwini MP
a5966.speech: Stated that the Pigg's Peak Hotel was once a major tourist attraction and a source of local employment ; said urgent action was needed to revive the hotel and ensure it once again contributes meaningfully to Eswatini's tourism industry ; said he hoped the report would help guide government's efforts to revitalise tourism in the northern region and strengthen Eswatini's position as a preferred destination for travellers.

a6023.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
a6023.speech: Claimed that the aborted United States Agency for International Development (USAID) funded terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram.

a6023.speaker: Ali Ndume, Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District and former Chairman of the Senate Committee on Army
a6023.speech: Has asked the Federal Government to probe US Congressman Scott Perry's claim: "You can't say it's just an allegation; it's more than that." ; "That's why the Nigerian government and the National Assembly, especially, need to look into it to investigate and verify the veracity of such a very weighty allegation." ; Said the Nigerian government should be interested in the US congressman's revelation, considering that there had been suspicions that foreign humanitarian agencies operating in Nigeria's insurgent-ridden North-East zone sponsored terrorist activities ; "This development is very worrisome, especially because one of the terrorist organisations mentioned by Scott Perry is Boko Haram, and Boko Haram has ravaged not only the North-East but even (other parts of) Nigeria." ; "You can remember Boko Haram bombed the police headquarters and the UN office in Abuja, and the casualties were enormous. So, the Nigerian government must be interested." ; "I'm worried, but the Nigerian security agencies have raised this indirectly several times. Even the Borno State government was wary of the operations of the NGOs." ; "I remember during the period of (Lieutenant General Tukur) Buratai, the Nigerian Army got intelligence and even raided the office of USAID or United Nations in Maiduguri. There was also a time when the governor got intelligence and security agencies raided one NGO that was providing training to some of their staff on how to use guns."

a6083.speaker: Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd)
a6083.speech: Has clarified that there is no discrepancy between its crude oil production figures and those supplied by the regulatory agency, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Company (NUPRC).

a6083.speaker: Olufemi O. Soneye, Chief Corporate Communications Officer, NNPC Ltd. (statement)
a6083.speech: According to a statement, the seeming disparity is as a result of the difference in the period of coverage in the reports – whereas the NNPC Ltd's figure was the peak production for October 2024, the NUPRC's figure was the average production for September 2024.

a6083.speaker: Gbenga Komolafe, Chief Executive Officer of NUPRC (represented by Enorense Amadasu, Executive Commissioner, Development & Production)
a6083.speech: Disclosed that Nigeria's crude oil output, including condensate, increased by 16.56 percent to 1.8mbpd in October 2024, from 1.54 million bpd in September 2024: “This represents an increase of 253,710bpd to reach 1.8 million bpd in October, up from 1.54 million bpd in September 2024, representing 16.56 percent month on-month rise”.

a6083.speaker: Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Company (NUPRC)
a6083.speech: Also confirmed at the NAPE event that the 1.8mbpd feat pushed Nigeria's production beyond the 1.5mbpd quota of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

a6112.speaker: Abraham Lincoln (1809-1865)
a6112.speech: Would have said 'You can fool some of the people all of the time, and all of the people some of the time, but you cannot fool all the people all the time.'

a6112.speaker: Education officials
a6112.speech: A remarkable number of citizens, especially education officials, lament that many trained teachers have irrelevant teaching qualifications.

a6112.speaker: Those in power (Namibian authorities)
a6112.speech: Argue that Namibia is not the only country with qualified unemployed teachers; some cynically retort that "the situation is worse in other countries than it is in Namibia"; others deny that government is "responsible for employing teachers, including those on government scholarships."

a6112.speaker: Political party leaders
a6112.speech: Call the practice of giving government jobs to loyal supporters, friends and relatives loyal cadre deployment.

a6112.speaker: Constitution of Namibia
a6112.speech: Prohibits the discrimination of any person on the grounds of sex, race, colour, ethnic origin, religion, creed or social or economic status.

a6183.speaker: Authorities (Burkina Faso government)
a6183.speech: Said this ambitious project falls within the framework of the Agropastoral and Fisheries Offensive (OAPH) 2023-2025 and aims to endow Burkina Faso with an autonomous veterinary pharmaceutical industry.

a6183.speaker: Captain Aboubacar Nacro, Director General of Veterinary Services
a6183.speech: Said this initiative responds to several structural challenges of the livestock sub-sector: dependence on imports of veterinary medicines, high costs, the inadequacy of packaging adapted to local realities, and weak support for research in animal health ; said that with this infrastructure Burkina Faso is crossing a decisive threshold towards animal health sovereignty, by equipping its livestock sector with modern disease prevention tools, in the service of food security and rural economic development.

a6287.speaker: Government of Mali
a6287.speech: Expressed its surprise and indignation following the publication, on 15 February, by the United States Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), announcing the cancellation of a $14 million grant (about 8.8 billion CFA francs) originally intended to support social cohesion in Mali.

a6287.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (communiqué dated 24 February 2025)
a6287.speech: Sought to clarify the country's position on the matter and to denounce once again the use of official development assistance as an “instrument of destabilisation”.

a6287.speaker: US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) publication of 15 February
a6287.speech: Announced the cancellation of a $14 million grant (about 8.8 billion CFA francs) originally intended to support social cohesion in Mali.

a6654.speaker: Wall Street Journal (citing unnamed sources)
a6654.speech: Reported that the US has suspended funding for any new arms sales to Ukraine, saying that Washington "has stopped financing new weapons sales to Ukraine and is considering freezing weapons shipments from US stockpiles."

a6654.speaker: Axios
a6654.speech: Claimed that Trump would conduct a meeting Monday afternoon on the Ukraine conflict, "including a possible suspension of US military aid", and that Vice President J.D. Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, National Security Adviser Mike Waltz and several other senior officials are expected to take part.

a6654.speaker: The Washington Post (citing an anonymous senior US official)
a6654.speech: Carried a similar report on Monday, saying that Trump would hold a meeting later in the day to "discuss whether to end military assistance to Ukraine" ; claimed that aside from stopping arms and equipment deliveries to Kiev, the termination of intelligence sharing and training for Ukrainian troops and pilots is also under consideration.

a6654.speaker: Vladimir Zelensky, Ukrainian leader
a6654.speech: On Sunday predicted that a peace agreement between his country and Russia "is still very, very far away" ; expressed confidence that despite his acrimonious exchange with Trump and Vance at the White House on Friday, "Ukraine has a strong enough partnership with the United States of America" to keep the aid flowing.

a6654.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (post on his Truth Social platform)
a6654.speech: Described Zelensky's remarks as the "worst statement that could have been made by Zelenskyy" ; warned that "America will not put up with it for much longer", adding that Zelensky "doesn't want there to be Peace as long as he has America's backing."

a6654.speaker: Mike Waltz, US National Security Advisor (speaking to Fox News)
a6654.speech: Hinted that the "American people's patience is not unlimited, their wallets are not unlimited, and our stockpiles and munitions are not unlimited" ; described Zelensky as the "problem" due to his refusal to "talk peace": "Time is not on his side. Time is not on the side of just forever continuing this conflict."

a6654.speaker: Howard Lutnick, US Commerce Secretary (interview with Fox News)
a6654.speech: Said that the Ukrainian leader had been told in no uncertain terms during Friday's meeting with Trump that further financial support would be contingent on Ukraine's willingness to negotiate peace with Russia.

a6707.speaker: Bok Kang, Korean Ambassador in Mozambique
a6707.speech: Said the aid will provide urgent relief to the internally displaced people in Cabo Delgado ; "In addition to meeting immediate humanitarian needs, this support will also contribute to long-term solutions through regional development efforts, where part of this funding will strengthen the IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix, which helps to monitor displaced populations and improve response efforts" ; believes that the collaboration between South Korea and IOM strengthens the collective capacity to meet the immediate and long-term needs of displaced communities in Mozambique ; "We trust that the IOM will continue to be dedicated to its work, delivering significant results that will make a real difference to the lives of the people affected. Korea continues its commitment to supporting Mozambique, not only in humanitarian assistance, but also in the development of various projects, especially the construction of the Quelimane Central Hospital, the supply of essential medical equipment and training for health professionals"

a6707.speaker: Dinis Dinis, manager of the Shelter Programme in Cabo Delgado
a6707.speech: Explained that, in addition to Korea, the project relies on a variety of other donors, involved in rebuilding infrastructure and human dignity, which means that a large investment is needed in order to reach the largest number of displaced people ; "So far, needs have been identified in the districts of Mocimboa da Praia and Metuge"

a6733.speaker: European Union
a6733.speech: The European Union on Friday confirmed that it is ready to support Mozambique in its fight against the islamist terrorists who have been rampaging through several districts in the northern province of Cabo Delgado since October 2017.

a6733.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a6733.speech: a request made by the Mozambican government in September, asking for humanitarian and logistical support, and specialist training for the Mozambican defence and security forces.

a6733.speaker: Antonio Sánchez-Benedito Gaspar, EU ambassador to Mozambique
a6733.speech: “In this letter”, Gaspar told reporters, “the European Union confirms its full solidarity with the people and government of Mozambique, in the current situation of armed violence that the country is living through in Cabo Delgado” ; The EU, he added, is committing itself “first to combat this terrorism, and at the same time to provide support for the population” ; The EU support rests on three pillars, namely humanitarian assistance, security and development.

a6733.speaker: Antonio Sánchez-Benedito Gaspar, EU ambassador to Mozambique
a6733.speech: he ruled out sending European troops to Mozambique. “The Mozambican government was very clear, and this is not on the agenda”, he said. “What is on the agenda are other questions which are also very important for strengthening the capacities of the Mozambican state to combat violence in the north” ; He added that all the requests made by the Mozambican government have met with a positive response.

a6733.speaker: Antonio Sánchez-Benedito Gaspar (@SBeneditoEU), social media post
a6733.speech: “Great meeting with MFA Minister Macamo to deliver @JosepBorrellF letter in response to the GoM request for assistance in addressing extremist violence in #CaboDelgado. #EU positive response reiterates our commitment to humanitarian assistance, development and security.”

a6733.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (letter)
a6733.speech: a letter from Josep Borrell, the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, which he delivered to Mozambican Foreign Minister Veronica Macamo, confirming the EU's full solidarity with the people and government of Mozambique.

a6733.speaker: Mirko Manzoni, Personal Representative to Mozambique of UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a6733.speech: on Friday reiterated his appeal to the Junta’s leader, Mariano Nhongo, to join the current demobilisation of the Renamo militia. “All Mozambicans deserve to live without fear, and I firmly believe that peaceful resolution of the conflict through communication and dialogue is the only credible way of advancing”, he stressed.

a6733.speaker: Mirko Manzoni, Personal Representative to Mozambique of UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres (written declaration)
a6733.speech: Manzoni guaranteed that he remains committed to ensuring a definitive peace for Mozambique, and he invited all Mozambicans to play a role in achieving this objective. He said that the progress made so far in demobilising and disarming the Renamo militia and reintegrating its members into society was evidence of the will of the Mozambican people to guarantee a peaceful future. “I have witnessed first hand the hope and the relief felt by the former combatants, now that they finally have the opportunity to go home”, he added. “For me, it is obvious that there is no desire to return to the days of conflict”.

a6733.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, President of Mozambique
a6733.speech: responded immediately to Manzoni’s declaration, saying that he remains willing to continue the government’s dialogue with Renamo to ensure effective peace ; he urged the Renamo dissidents under Nhongo to lay down their weapons and join the demobilisation ; Nyusi declared that peace and security are fundamental requirements for economic growth. “I am available to lead this peace process here in Manica, and throughout the country”, he said. “I shall continue to collaborate with the Renamo leadership and I invite our brothers to join us to develop this country. The country needs all Mozambicans”.

a6733.speaker: Ossufo Momade, Renamo leader
a6733.speech: The same appeal [to lay down weapons and join the demobilisation] has also been made by Renamo leader Ossufo Momade.

a7033.speaker: Massoud Ali Mohammed, Zanzibar Minister at the President's Office, Regional Authority, Local Government and Special Departments (PORALG SD)
a7033.speech: Reaffirmed the Zanzibar government's commitment to supporting the USAID Kizazi Hodari Southern Zone Project and emphasized the government's recognition of the project's efforts in addressing the challenges faced by OVCs and youth: “This project operates at the grassroots level, directly impacting its participants. We understand the challenges faced by children living with HIV, particularly those who have lost their parents.” ; “The Zanzibar government deeply appreciates these efforts, and we are committed to providing all the support necessary to ensure the success of your operations.”

a7033.speaker: Ruwayda Redfearn, Chief Executive Officer of Deloitte Africa
a7033.speech: Expressed her gratitude for the Zanzibar government's continued support and collaboration: “I'm very pleased with the level of support we've received while implementing this project. Working with various government ministries has ensured smooth operations. It is encouraging to see the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar's role in supporting the USAID KHSZ Project and its plans for sustaining these services in the future.”

a7033.speaker: Anne Muraya, Deloitte East Africa CEO
a7033.speech: Highlighted the core focus of the project: “The USAID Kizazi Hodari (Brave Generation) Southern Zone project is child-focused and family-centered, aiming to improve health, safety, education, and stability for OVCs and youth aged 0-17 in high HIV-burden communities. Women play a crucial role in driving this change, contributing significantly to the global 95-95-95 targets aimed at achieving sustained antiretroviral therapy and viral suppression by 2030.”

a7072.speaker: Country Strategy Paper (CSP) 2025-2030 consultations
